title: Time-bounded computation implies computation
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over an alphabet $\Sigma$, let $f$ map words over $\Sigma$ to words over $\Sigma$, and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. If on every input $x$, $M$ halts with output $f(x)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps, then $M$ computes $f$; that is, on every input it eventually halts with output $f(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over $\Sigma$
$f$ maps words over $\Sigma$ to words over $\Sigma$
replaced:
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over an alphabet $\Sigma$.  If $M$ computes
the string function $f \colon \Sigma^{*} \to \Sigma^{*}$ in time
$T \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ (halting within $T(\abs{x})$ steps on
every input $x$ with $f(x)$ on its output tape), then $M$ computes $f$, i.e.\
on every input it eventually halts with the value of $f$ on its output tape.
